title: Lena and the Parish
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Parish is exhumed for a tercentenary reburial and found empty, cathedral archivist Sebastian Galloway is the only person with keys to the crypt — making her both prime suspect and reluctant investigator. Her digging uncovers that Edmund's descendants staged his death thirty years ago to hide a murder, weaving alibis that the statute of limitations is about to render untouchable. As Sebastian closes in, she discovers her own late mother was the missing witness whose silence was bought with the inheritance that raised her. In the end, Sebastian chooses truth over family: she publishes the archive evidence before the statute expires, sending the surviving conspirator to trial and finally laying an empty coffin — and her mother's memory — to rest.
about_author: Vesper Fairweather is a former church archivist from the Yorkshire coast who left records-keeping for fiction after cataloguing one too many sealed doors. She writes mysteries about small towns that keep their history locked, and about the people who inherit the keys.

chapters.title: The Tercentenary Exhumation
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The town gathers to move founder Edmund Parish to a marble tomb, and Sebastian unlocks the crypt she alone maintains — revealing an empty coffin. The crowd's awe curdles into suspicion aimed at her. Emotional beat: pride in her order and craft shattering into public disgrace.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Dust
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Under police pressure, she audits her own accession logs and finds a gap: a box of Parish family papers removed in 1995, signed out by her mother, then a cathedral employee. Emotional beat: the first crack — the case may be personal.

chapters.title: The Heirs of Parish
chapters.summary: Sebastian interviews the founder's descendants: matriarch Vivian Parish, her brittle son Aldous, and granddaughter Tamsin, who hints the family 'agreed long ago never to dig.' Each alibi is polished, rehearsed, thirty years old. Emotional beat: the uncanny smoothness of lies kept too long.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with a flashback to her mother's final year. She searches her childhood home and finds the missing box hidden in a floor cavity — inside, a ledger and an unsent confession letter naming a victim no one ever reported missing. Emotional beat: grief reopening as betrayal.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The letter, written in her mother's hand, confesses she witnessed something at Parish Hall in 1994 but stops before naming anyone — the final page torn out. Meanwhile the statute expires in six weeks. Emotional beat: urgency fusing with dread.

chapters.title: Aldous Recants
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. Terrified by Sebastian's questions, he nearly confesses to her that his father never died naturally — but Vivian interrupts, and he retreats into denial. That night he burns a bundle of letters. Emotional beat: cowardice at war with conscience.

chapters.title: The Crypt's Second Door
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Studying mason's marks, she finds a bricked-up secondary passage into the crypt — used recently, mortar still pale. Whoever emptied the coffin did it from inside the family's private chapel. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing the prey has been close all along.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She offers Sebastian the torn final page in exchange for leaving the Parish name intact — her mother's alibi, her grandmother's crime, her inheritance at stake. Sebastian refuses. Emotional beat: the seduction and refusal of complicity.

chapters.title: Night in the Undercroft
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Confronted in the crypt, Vivian admits she killed the man her husband Edmund had framed and destroyed, and that Sebastian's mother took hush money to raise her daughter — the inheritance was the price of survival. When Vivian moves to seal the passage, Aldous intervenes. Emotional beat: terror, truth, and an unexpected ally.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She files the ledger and confession with the coroner hours before the statute expires; Vivian is charged, Aldous testifies, and the town reburies an empty coffin with a stone that finally tells the truth. Sebastian adds her mother's letter to the archive, unsealed. Emotional beat: costly peace — inheritance refused, memory kept honest.
